title: Chess Endgames: Checkmating With Few Pieces
subject: thinking

sections.body: An endgame is the last part of a game when few pieces are left. Knowing basic endgames helps you turn an advantage into a win.

Which pieces can force checkmate against a lone king? A king and queen can. A king and rook can. A king and a single knight cannot, and neither can a king and a single bishop. With so little material, the game is a draw.
The method is to push the enemy king to the edge of the board, because a king in the middle has too many squares. Use your king to help: it must come close to take squares away from the enemy king.

The great danger is stalemate. If you give the lone king no moves while not giving check, the game is drawn. A good habit before each move: 'Does the enemy king still have a legal move, or is it in check?'
Set up a king and queen against a king and practise driving the enemy king to the edge. After each move, check that you have not stalemated.
Drawn endgames and stalemate tricks are very common in beginners' games. If your child keeps drawing won positions, practise king and queen against king over and over.

quiz.q: Which of these can force checkmate against a lone king?
options: A king and a single knight
A king and a single bishop
hints: Think about which pieces control a lot of squares.
A lone knight or a lone bishop is not enough, on its own.
Example: with a king and rook against a king you can force mate by driving the king to the edge. Decide which option is that strong.
quiz.explain: A king and queen can force checkmate. A king and one knight, or a king and one bishop, cannot.

quiz.q: You have a king and queen against a lone king. Black's king on h8 has no legal move, but is not in check. What is the result of the game?
options: A win for White by checkmate
hints: It is not in check, and it has no legal move.
Example: a king that is attacked and cannot escape is checkmated. Is that this case, or the other case where the king is simply stuck?
quiz.explain: Black is not in check and has no legal moves. That is stalemate, a draw, even though White has far more pieces.

quiz.q: Why is it a good idea to drive the lone enemy king to the edge of the board?
options: On the edge it has fewer squares to run to, so it is easier to trap
The edge squares are worth more points than the squares in the middle of the board
Kings are not allowed to stay in the middle of the board
hints: Count how many squares a king can reach in the middle, then at the edge.
A king in the middle can step to 8 squares. On the edge it has fewer.
Example: a king in a corner can step to only 3 squares. Think about why that helps you.
quiz.explain: A king on the edge has fewer squares, so it is easier to take them all away and give checkmate.
